groups.summary: Every diagnostic the engine reports while it lowers sz.
Emitted classes this project's Tailwind generates no CSS for.
Opacity modifiers on a colour whose theme value color-mix() cannot dim.
Values that emit a class setting another property than their key sets.
Theme tokens whose name a built-in utility also uses.
sz keys the build removed because a later key in the same object covers them.
className classes the build removed because an sz class on the element covers them.

diagnostics.summary: A key no sz table knows, likely a typo.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is not an sz property.
diagnostics.help: {spellingHint} For a custom utility, define it with Tailwind's `@utility`.
diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing unless Tailwind serves that utility.

diagnostics.summary: An alias of a key, with the canonical spelling to write.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is an alias of `{canonical}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
diagnostics.help: write `{canonical}`.

diagnostics.summary: A key that was removed or replaced, with what to write instead.

text.runtime-alias: `{key}` was removed, and nothing is emitted for its runtime value.
text.sugar-replaced: `{key}` was replaced, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.sugar: The boolean shorthand `{key}` was removed, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.removed: `{key}` was removed, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.replaced: `{key}` was replaced, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.runtime-alias: write {canonicalAllowed} on `{canonical}`, and the other values on {groups}.

diagnostics.summary: A numeric key, the mark of an array or spread passed as an sz object.
diagnostics.text: `sz` received a numeric key `{key}`, and its value is ignored.
diagnostics.help: pass an object of sz keys here; a numeric key usually means an array or a spread was passed in its place.

diagnostics.summary: A value a closed-enum key does not take.

text.sibling-group: `{key}: {value}` is not a `{key}` value; its class `{bare}` belongs to `{ {groupKey}: {groupLiteral} }`.
text.css-value: `{key}: '{value}'` is a CSS value, and `{key}-{value}` generates no CSS.
text.font-style: `{key}: '{value}'` has no Tailwind class, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.font-smoothing: `{key}: '{value}'` has no Tailwind class, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.sibling-group: write `{ {groupKey}: {groupLiteral} }`, so it combines with the other groups instead of resetting them.
help.font-style: use `'italic'` or `'normal'`; for any other style, such as oblique, write `css: { fontStyle: '{value}' }`.

note.dead: the class `{bare}` is still emitted, and it styles nothing unless a rule of your own matches it.

diagnostics.summary: A colour key given its opacity in a string, which emits nothing; the object form takes it.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{color}/{opacity}'` emits nothing: a string value cannot carry a slash opacity.
diagnostics.help: use the object form: `{ color: '{color}', op: {opacity} }`.

diagnostics.summary: A spacing value off Tailwind's quarter-step scale.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: {value}` is not on Tailwind's spacing scale, so the class generates no CSS.
diagnostics.help: use a quarter step such as `1.25`, `1.5` or `1.75`, or a unit value such as `'{value}rem'`.

diagnostics.summary: A font weight written as a numeric string.
diagnostics.text: `weight: '{value}'` is a numeric string, so `font-{value}` generates no CSS.
diagnostics.help: write `weight: {value}` as a number; it emits `font-[{value}]`.

diagnostics.summary: A border style on one side, which Tailwind cannot express.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{value}'` emits nothing: Tailwind has no per-side border style.
diagnostics.help: use `borderStyle: '{value}'` for every side, or a number on `{key}` for the width.

diagnostics.summary: An object on a key that names a property, not a variant.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is a property, and its object `{ {nestedKeys} }` emits `{key}:*` classes that match no Tailwind variant and generate no CSS.
diagnostics.help: move the nested keys up a level; for colour opacity, write `{ color: '…', op: … }`.

diagnostics.summary: An object on a csszyx-owned key that is not a variant.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is not a variant, so its object emits `{key}:` classes that generate no CSS.
diagnostics.help: a `--*` key takes a declaration value; `container` takes `true`.

diagnostics.summary: A field a structured value (a mask layer) does not take.
diagnostics.text: `{owner}` has no field `{member}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
diagnostics.help: `{owner}` takes `{ {allowed} }`.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value on a key with no CSS-variable utility.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` cannot take a runtime value: Tailwind has no utility for this key that reads a CSS variable.
diagnostics.help: name the values with `szv()`, or use `dynamic()` for open-ended data.
diagnostics.note: no class or variable is emitted for `{key}`.

diagnostics.summary: A spread in an sz object the build cannot resolve.
diagnostics.text: This `sz` object spreads a value the build cannot read, so the object falls back to the runtime and may render no styles in production.
diagnostics.help: use the array form: `sz={[x, { … }]}` in place of `sz={{ ...x, … }}`.

diagnostics.summary: A props spread that may override the style sz emits.
diagnostics.text: This element spreads props that may carry `style`, and the `style` that `sz` writes can replace it.
diagnostics.help: move the spread `style` to an explicit `style` prop, so csszyx merges both values.

diagnostics.summary: An szs slot map the build cannot read, or one on a host element.

text.host-element: `szs` has no effect on a host element; it maps the slot names of a custom component.
text.unreadable-slot: A slot value in `szs` could not be read at build time, so no slot classes were compiled.

help.host-element: remove `szs`, or move it to the custom component whose slots it names.
help.unreadable-slot: write every slot as an identifier key with a static object literal or class string; for a value known only at runtime, pass the class string `dynamic()` returns.

diagnostics.summary: An szRecover value the build cannot read.
diagnostics.note: no `data-sz-recovery-token` is written for this element.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime className beside sz, which sz overrides.
diagnostics.text: `sz` wins over the runtime `className` on this element in any attribute order, so a caller's `className` cannot override these styles.
diagnostics.help: state the order in one `sz` array: `sz={[{ … }, className]}` for the caller to win, `sz={[className, { … }]}` for these styles to win.

diagnostics.summary: An element with more than one sz attribute, merged in order.
diagnostics.text: `<{elementName}>` carries {count} `sz` attributes, merged in order as `sz={[first, …, last]}`: the later one wins for each property.
diagnostics.help: fold them into one `sz` array, so the order is written down.

diagnostics.summary: Class names and sz on more than one side of a spread.
diagnostics.text: `<{elementName}>` has class names or `sz` on more than one side of a spread; in React, Preact, Solid and Qwik the last class attribute replaces the others, so {earlier} will not apply there.
diagnostics.help: write them in one `sz` array after {spreadPlace}, in the order that should win: `sz={[{example}]}`.
diagnostics.note: Vue JSX merges every class, so every side applies there.

diagnostics.summary: A value that moved to another key, with the key to write.

text.value: `{key}: {value}` moved to `{movedKey}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.mask-layer: `mask: '{value}'` names a gradient layer, which moved to `{layerKey}`, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.mask-layer: write this layer on `{layerKey}`; `mask` takes only `none`, a `url()` or a CSS variable.

diagnostics.summary: A stand-alone keyword written before a group key that replaces it.
diagnostics.text: `{global}: {value}` comes before `{group}` in one sz object, so `{group}` replaces it and the `{global}` value styles nothing.
diagnostics.help: to override the group, layer it: `sz={[base, { {global}: '{value}' }]}`.
diagnostics.note: a spread such as `{ ...base, {global}: '{value}' }` keeps the same key order, so it does not fix this.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value beside the other side of its key family.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` takes a runtime value beside `{other}` in one sz object, so both classes can ship and Tailwind's stylesheet order decides which applies, whatever the object's order.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime fallback whose classes were never collected.

text.szv: The `szv` config cannot be read at build time: {fallbackReason}.

help.szv: pass the config inline, or as a module-level const object literal.

note.sz: its classes were not collected, so Tailwind generates CSS for them only if another source names them.
note.szr: its classes were not collected, so Tailwind generates CSS for them only if another source names them.
note.szv: none of its variant classes were collected, so they generate no CSS.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime fallback whose classes were still collected.

text.sz-array-element: This `sz` array element is an object literal with a runtime value, so the whole element is resolved at runtime.

help.sz-array-element: use finite literal ternary branches where you can, or move the runtime values to `dynamic()`.

note.sz: the runtime still turns the value into classes.
note.sz-array-element: its classes are still collected, best-effort.

diagnostics.summary: A merge table this engine cannot read, so nothing merged.

text.unreadable: The merge table is not one this engine reads ({error}), so no sz key was merged with a later key that covers it.
text.format-mismatch: The merge table is in format {tableFormat}, and this engine reads format {mergeTableFormat}, so no sz key was merged with a later key that covers it.

diagnostics.help: install the same csszyx version of every `@csszyx` package, then rebuild; under Turbopack, delete `.csszyx/merge-table.json` and run `csszyx next prebuild`.
diagnostics.note: every class is kept, as before 0.18, so `{ pb: 2, p: 4 }` emits both and the stylesheet order decides.

diagnostics.summary: A file the parser rejected, which contributes no classes.

text.summary: csszyx could not parse this file (syntax errors: {errorCount}).
text.panicked: The parser stopped at a syntax error it could not recover from.
text.expression: This `sz` value could not be parsed as a JavaScript expression.
text.prescan: This file failed to parse, so the build collected no classes from it.

help.syntax: fix the syntax at this position.
help.summary: fix the syntax errors reported for this file.
help.panicked: fix the syntax error reported for this file.
help.expression: write the value as an object literal, such as `{ p: 4 }`.
help.prescan: fix the syntax error, or check that the file extension matches its contents.

note.expression: the attribute is left as written, and no class is generated for it.
note.prescan: its classes generate no CSS unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A file nested deeper than the parser guard allows.
diagnostics.text: Source nesting exceeds {maxNestingDepth} levels (found {depth}).
diagnostics.help: flatten the structure; nesting this deep usually comes from `sz` or JSX over-nested by hand or by generated code.
diagnostics.note: the file is left unchanged and contributes no classes.

diagnostics.summary: An sz attribute whose value the engine cannot read.
diagnostics.text: This `sz` attribute has no value, or a JSX element as its value.
diagnostics.help: give `sz` a value in braces, such as `sz={{ p: 4 }}`, or remove it.
diagnostics.note: the attribute is left as written; the rest of the file is still transformed.

diagnostics.summary: A file over the AST budget, left unchanged.

text.transform: The file exceeds the AST node budget.
text.prescan: The file exceeds the AST node budget, so the build collected no classes from it.

diagnostics.help: raise `build.astBudgetLimit` in the csszyx plugin options, or split the file.

note.transform: the file is left unchanged, and none of its classes are collected.
note.prescan: their CSS is not generated unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A CSS variable mangleVars could not hoist to a component.

text.no-lca: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: its {usageCount} usages share no common JSX ancestor.
text.non-host-ancestor: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: the common ancestor of its {usageCount} usages cannot take a `style` prop.
text.max-depth: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: one of its {usageCount} usages sits more than {maxDepth} levels below their common ancestor.

diagnostics.note: each element that uses it keeps its own scoped variable, and every class is still emitted.

diagnostics.summary: A colour object with a slash opacity in `color`; the object takes it in `op`.

text.op-given: `{key}: { color: '{base}/{opacity}{important}', op: {op} }` sets opacity twice; a colour object takes its opacity in `op`, not in `color`.
text.op-absent: `{key}: { color: '{base}/{opacity}{important}' }` puts the opacity in `color`; a colour object takes it in `op`.

note.op-given: the class uses `op: {op}`; the `/{opacity}` in `color` is ignored.

diagnostics.summary: A negative value on a key Tailwind serves no negative utility for.
An emitted class this project's Tailwind generates no CSS for.
An engine diagnostic the text matcher could not name, from a lane that drops its code.
Tailwind entries in one project that set different prefixes.
A value that emits a class setting another property than its key sets.
An opacity modifier on a colour whose theme value color-mix() cannot dim.
A theme token whose name a built-in utility also uses.
An sz key the build removed because a later key in the same object covers it.
A className class the build removed because an sz class on the element covers it.
A recovery manifest that is not valid JSON or not in the recovery format.
A mangle map on the page that is not a plain map of class names, so it is ignored.
A mangle census on the page that is not a valid map, so nothing was verified.
A mangle map whose hash differs from the checksum it was built with.
A page with a mangle checksum but no census or map to recompute it from.
A page without Web Crypto, so the mangle checksum cannot be recomputed.
A hydration check that threw on an element and stopped.
A hydration mismatch on an element without an szRecover directive.
An szRecover="dev-only" element in a production build, where its recovery is off.
A hydration mismatch the runtime recovered by rendering on the client.
A merge table in a format this runtime does not read, so szcn merges nothing.
A run with no merge table, so szcn removes only exact repeats.
A raw sz object that reached the runtime because its file was not compiled.
A registerSzcnGroups call, which no longer changes what szcn merges.
A theme token defined under two namespaces that share one class prefix.
A has/pick/omit selector that can never match a token.
A selector name that is no category or class prefix csszyx knows.
A splitBox placement written with a variant or marker, which never matches.
A peer class splitBox kept on the frame although its base belongs inside.
A class or raw CSS splitBox cannot classify, placed on the fallback node.
A scrolling content node whose height nothing bounds, so it grows instead.
A rounded frame that does not clip its scrolling content.
A hiding class placed on the content node, which leaves the frame visible.
A part of an szv config that does not have the shape szv reads.
An sz object at runtime nested deeper than the depth limit.
A key in an szv config that csszyx never reads, such as __proto__.
A selection that names a variant the szv config does not declare.
A selection that gives a variant a value it has no styles for.
An sz object from szv() used as a class string, which renders "[object Object]".
A session in which dynamic() has injected so many classes the CSSOM keeps growing.
An arbitrary value dynamic() dropped because it could inject CSS.
A runtime value that is not a boolean on a key only a boolean can toggle.
A runtime value of a type no CSS value can be resolved from.
Development warnings that cover only the files a page loads; csszyx check scans all.
More findings of one kind than a run lists; the rest are counted, not printed.
An sz attribute string that does not parse.
An options argument that is not the one object the call takes.
An sz object passed to a string helper before the lowering module is loaded.
An sz object passed to a lite-runtime helper, which cannot lower objects.
A class string passed to splitBoxSz, which takes sz objects.
Two builds sharing one runtime that registered different Tailwind prefixes.
A dynamic manifest the browser could not fetch.
A native engine that is missing, cannot load, or predates this compiler.
A wasm engine that failed to load.
A native engine csszyx migrate needs and cannot load; migrate has no wasm lane.
An engine built from other source than the compiler that loads it.
A @csszyx/runtime at another version than the plugin that lowers for it.
A peer package csszyx needs that does not resolve from the project.
A project where generate-types finds no loadable Tailwind CSS v3.
An input to csszyx explain that is not one sz expression the build lowers.
A Vue or Svelte file whose template sz has errors, each reported with its own code.
A template sz value only known at runtime, which a template cannot resolve.
A Vue or Svelte file its own compiler cannot parse, so no sz in it gets a class.
A Vue template in a language other than HTML, which csszyx does not read.
An installed Svelte older than 5, whose markup csszyx does not read.
An installed `ignore` package that no longer reads .gitignore the way csszyx needs.
A state csszyx should never reach: a csszyx bug to report.
A call into the engine that threw.
A csszyx.config with problems, each reported with its own code.
A rule id no diagnostic, kind or group has, likely a typo.
A rule id for a runtime line or a throw, whose level csszyx.config cannot set.
A rule id csszyx no longer reports, with the id that replaced it.
A rule set to something other than off, info, warn or error.
A diagnostics preset other than recommended or atomic.
A field csszyx.config does not read.
A csszyx.config field whose value does not have the shape it takes.
An override glob that is absolute or steps out of the root, so it never matches.
A second csszyx.config file beside the one csszyx reads.
A csszyx.config that could not be loaded, so the default levels apply.
A csszyx.config with no default export.
A saved diagnostic policy in a format this version does not read.
A Next safelist shard in a format this version does not read.
Findings at info a production build counted instead of listing.
Classes a build removed by merging, counted instead of listed.
A plugin option that was removed and is no longer read.
A build without its transform cache, because package versions did not resolve.
The parser a build runs, and whether it fell back from the native engine.
A project-wide input that changed, so a dev server recompiled every module.
A Tailwind prefix that changed during a watch build, which needs a restart.
A generated safelist csszyx could not write, so Tailwind misses its classes.
An @utility whose name another utility also claims, so Tailwind merges both.
Theme auto-scan turned on in a project without TypeScript configured.
production.mangle on the esbuild adapter, which turns mangling off.
A CSS selector the class mangler could not parse, left unmangled.
A production.manglePreserve entry that is not a class name or a prefix.
production.mangleGlobalVars options csszyx cannot apply.
A global-variable alias plan that renames a variable unsafely.
A CSS variable mangle map larger than its safety cap.
Classes that appeared after the mangle map was frozen.
A rule selecting on a class the build had already merged away.
A configured Tailwind stylesheet that does not exist.
A stylesheet reaching Tailwind that does not compile, so the prefix is unknown.
A Tailwind config path that does not exist.
A Tailwind config that threw while loading.
An @source line naming the old safelist file, which csszyx no longer writes.
The csszyx PostCSS plugin listed after Tailwind, which then never reads the safelist.
A negated pattern in an ignore list, which can only add paths.
A CSS source that kept changing while csszyx read it.
A client-only csszyx export imported into a Server Component.
A Next lane that runs before the Tailwind prefix was read.
A Next safelist state another live process holds the lock on.
A Next generation manifest that does not have the shape csszyx writes.
production.mangleVars on a Next lane that cannot mangle CSS variables.
A Turbopack production build whose safelist was not seeded by csszyx next prebuild.
A Next module that still holds sz syntax after the csszyx transform.
A Next safelist watcher whose first cycle did not complete.
A Next safelist watcher that threw while closing.
A source pattern that matched no file under the root.
A CLI option value outside the values the command takes.

removed.reason: The `code` of @csszyx/core's CsszyxNativeUnavailableError since 0.9.0, renamed to the kebab-case grammar every other code uses. No /e/ page: the old string breaks the URL grammar.
